questions.q: What are the Life-Force 8 in the summary?
a: Eight core desires that advertising should appeal to
Eight steps for writing a perfect headline
Eight kinds of advertising media to choose from
Eight rules for pricing a new product
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists the eight inborn desires, from survival to approval, that motivate far more purchases than anything else.

questions.q: What sequence does the summary say turns a desire into a sale?
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes how unmet needs create tension, which sparks desire and pushes the reader to act.

questions.q: What is the first step in crafting a persuasive headline?
a: Keep it as short as possible
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the most persuasive part, the greatest perk, should come first so readers keep going.

questions.q: About what share of people who see an ad read only the headline?
questions.why: Lesson 2 cites the estimate that most readers stop at the headline, which is why it has to grab attention.

questions.q: What does the summary claim about long copy?
a: It draws interested buyers in better than short copy
It scares most casual readers away
It works only for inexpensive products
It suits print better than online ads
questions.why: Lesson 3 argues that buyers hungry for details will keep reading, so longer copy can build more desire.
